method: Gallagher least-squares index of disproportionality, computed from the vote shares and seat counts already recorded for every legislative election in this atlas. Unlisted parties are folded into one residual bucket; an election whose listed vote shares total under 80% is not scored.

hubs.note: Levelling seats are explicitly there to hold the index down.
The purest large-country PR in the atlas, and reliably the lowest index.

hubs.chamber: 183 seats over 39 regional districts, three allocation tiers
hubs.note: Three tiers make the final result close to the national vote.
Threshold raised from 2% in 2014, which pushed small parties into joint lists.

hubs.chamber: 174 seats in 3-, 4- and 5-seat constituencies, single transferable vote
hubs.note: The only national PR-STV system in this atlas. Seats follow the final count, not first preferences.

hubs.chamber: 289 districts plus 176 by list in 11 blocs
hubs.note: SNTV multi-member districts until 1993.
The presidency is a separate two-round contest.
The 2023 reform removed overhang seats from 2025.
Panachage lets voters split a list across parties.
Split Dutch and French electorates; compulsory voting.
Switched between systems repeatedly since 2005.

hubs.chamber: Closed-list PR with a bonus to the largest coalition
hubs.note: Changed repeatedly: PR to 1993, mixed to 2005, bonus-PR, Rosatellum from 2017, and a new bonus-PR law legislated in 2026.

hubs.chamber: 230 seats over 22 districts, D'Hondt, closed lists
hubs.note: No national threshold, but districts range from two seats to forty-eight, so the small interior ones are effectively two-party.
Threshold cut from 10% in 2022.
The Senate is 100 single-member seats, decided in 2023 by an opposition pact rather than by vote share.
Small provinces elect two or three members, so the system is far less proportional than the label suggests.

hubs.chamber: 300 seats, PR with a bonus to the largest party
hubs.note: The bonus has been as large as fifty seats, was abolished for May 2023 and restored for June, which is why two votes six weeks apart produced different parliaments.

hubs.threshold: 12.5% of the roll to reach round two
hubs.note: PR was used once, in 1986.

hubs.chamber: Group representation constituencies, plurality by team
hubs.note: Multi-member blocs are won whole, which pushes the index high.

hubs.chamber: 72 electorates topped up to 120 from party lists
hubs.note: FPTP until 1993. The index falls off a cliff at 1996, which is the reform itself.

hubs.chamber: 400 seats, closed national and regional lists
hubs.note: No threshold at all.
Two referendums on changing it have failed at provincial level.
Unchanged since the last multi-member seats went in 1950.
Elections suspended under martial law.
The presidency additionally needs 25% in two-thirds of the states.
A semi-mixed top-up since 2020.
Preferential voting with compulsory turnout; the Senate uses STV.

hubs.chamber: 596 seats: individual constituencies plus absolute-majority closed lists
hubs.note: A list plurality takes every seat on the list, which is why the pro-government coalition has swept them since 2015.

hubs.chamber: 132 seats, half list half district in 2006
hubs.note: One competitive legislative election on record.
Not a competitive system: the index measures the arithmetic, not consent.
The largest FPTP electorate in the world.

hubs.chamber: 257 deputies, half renewed every two years
hubs.note: Presidential elections use a reduced-threshold runoff.
hubs.gapReason: This hub records single-winner contests, which have no seat share to compare a vote share against.

hubs.chamber: Indirect election to the National People's Congress
hubs.note: No competitive contest; listed for completeness.
hubs.gapReason: No election met the scoring rules; the commonest reason was: no vote shares recorded.

hubs.chamber: 720 seats, each member state its own system
hubs.note: Twenty-seven national systems reported as one chamber, so read the index as an aggregate.
hubs.gapReason: No election met the scoring rules; the commonest reason was: no parties recorded.

hubs.chamber: Presidency by simple plurality, one six-year term
hubs.note: No runoff, so pluralities under 40% have repeatedly been enough to win.
hubs.gapReason: This hub records single-winner contests, which have no seat share to compare a vote share against.

hubs.note: SNTV until 2008.
hubs.gapReason: This hub records single-winner contests, which have no seat share to compare a vote share against.

hubs.note: Districts are drawn by the states, so the index carries redistricting as well as the system.
hubs.gapReason: This hub records single-winner contests, which have no seat share to compare a vote share against.

hubs.chamber: Conclave of cardinal electors, two-thirds majority
hubs.note: Not a polity-wide ballot, so it carries no index.
hubs.gapReason: This hub records single-winner contests, which have no seat share to compare a vote share against.
